findings.defect: global_check_refined_ge_grid is True by construction. The coarse-grid global argmax is always a grid local maximum, so it is always order[0]. Nelder-Mead starts with [0,0] in its initial simplex and returns the best vertex, so the refined correlation is always >= the full-map score at that axis. The field and the test assertion therefore check nothing about global optimality. The real evidence is the dense axis grid with closed-form roll, n_grid_local_maxima of 2-4, and best_other_basin_corr <= 0.86.

lane_resolution.change: Removed the field that was true by construction (global_check_refined_ge_grid). s4_bjs_comparator.py gains global_check(), which fit_rotation now runs by default. It does not reuse the fit's starting points: a finer HEALPix axis grid (nside 2*grid_nside, i.e. 32) on the coarse map, up to 8 of its local maxima refined by Nelder-Mead on the full map, plus 8 seeded random restarts (seed 20261124). It records corr_check_max - corr_best against a tolerance of 1e-9, fixed before the runs. The refinement code is factored out with identical numerics. The production fits were not rerun. Instead, the new script s4_posthoc_checks.py applied the same check to the saved maps of all 96 recorded fits (48 production, 48 Richardson). Results: max(corr_check)-corr_best = 1.1e-15, all pass, every fit has at least 2 checks in its own basin, and the best corr outside the fit basin is 0.866 at most. The recorded corr_spline is reproduced to 1.7e-15 at every recorded axis. Tests: the synthetic fit asserts excess <= 1e-9. A new test passes a wrong-basin 'best' to the check and asserts excess > 1e-3 and passes=False. A summary test asserts 96/96 checked and passing.

findings.defect: The lane publishes the Codazzi map with the documented meaning kappa q = +M sigma, the sign stated in the codazzi_tilt_rhs.py comment. The code settles which sign is right, and it is the production one. In htt/bass/background/convention_bridge.py:403-409, q_i = T^{0i} and D_j sigma^j_i + kappa q_i = 0. tilted_bianchi_state.py:150 has 'matrix @ shear_stf5 = -kappa*q_total' and :837-839 has G^{0i} = -D_j sigma^j_i = kappa T^{0i}. This matches Ellis–van Elst / Tsagas–Challinor–Maartens: D^b sigma_ab = (2/3) D_a Theta - q_a. It also matches the WE97/HBW01 form q = 3 sigma a - eps sigma n, which the lane's own test shows equals -div sigma. The comment at codazzi_tilt_rhs.py:359 is only a comment; that module's executable gate is a Friedmann-slack surrogate. The executable code with the opposite sign is constraints.codazzi_constraint_residual (div sigma - kappa q). That function drives initial_conditions' Codazzi projection, which therefore targets div sigma = +kappa q. This is a pre-existing sign inconsistency that R108 surfaced but labelled an open owner question, and R108 adopted the wrong-signed convention for its own output.

findings.defect: The K-matched controls are close to degenerate by construction. 2MRS is an apparent-magnitude cut, so most K-bin x cz x inclusion strata are entirely 2MRS members. As a result, 2773 of 3983 (69.6%) excluded rows at 0.25 mag and 2269 of 3983 (57.0%) at 0.5 mag are excluded in every control replicate. For the complement, the figures are 4057 of 4902 (82.8%) and 3034 of 4902 (61.9%). Each control differs from the observed exclusion only in the 1210 (or 1714) mixed-strata rows, so agreement between observed and control is largely built in. The R106 non-comparability criterion still fails under K-matching: the raw mark zero-point z is -6.9 to -9.0 for 2MRS and +5.3 to +7.9 for the complement. Even so, _run passes comparable=True unconditionally. summarize() then drops the comparable/degenerate flags, so the published blocks carry no comparability status beside the R106 references, which were flagged not comparable.

lane_resolution.change: Comparability is now set from the data. A hard-coded flag no longer decides it. In scripts/r108/cf4_kband_contrast.py, apply_comparability() overwrites the R106 label fields of every scored block and every R106 reference block. The threshold is Z_COMPARABLE=3, the same 3 sd line R106 used. Rules: (a) test_only (per fold key) and drop are comparable iff |raw mark zero-point z| < 3. (b) drop_recentered_czbin is comparable iff the residual member-minus-non-member split, on R105-selected rows inside the 2000 km/s recentring bins at the strata's own matching resolution, has |z| < 3. Resolutions: r106 = per cz bin; k0.25 and k0.5 = 2000 km/s x Ktot 0.25 or 0.5 mag cells. The z uses the R106 heterogeneity combination with the inflated error. That split is what czbin recentring cannot remove. findings.defect: At l=2 the integrator is 7.7% below CAMB counts_density for the z~1 window and 2.5% below for the z~0.5 window. The summary's own power-law extrapolation gives 22% and 7% at l=1. The CAMB side was never varied, yet the summary note attributes the gap without having tested CAMB.

lane_resolution.change: radio_theory_c1.py has a new v3_low_l_systematic() (tested). For each V3 window it fits a power law to |rel| over l=2..10 and extrapolates it to l=1, and s is the maximum over windows. The integrator is below CAMB at every tested l, so the systematic is one-sided upward: factor_up = 1/(1-s) and factor_down = 1. I used 1/(1-s) rather than the reviewer's 1+s because it is the CAMB-like value if the deficit is a fractional deficit of the integrator, and it is the more conservative choice. The function fails closed if s >= 0.5. THEORY_C1.json gains V3_low_l_systematic and envelope.<pv>.with_V3_low_l_systematic (extended/primary max, differential pair max and the Minkowski 4max, each times factor_up). findings.defect: RACS g_diff dipole powers are fed into the NVSS p(C1) machinery labelled 'empirical_independent'.
